uncertain.note: page quality: this is the CUDL colour scan and it is clean and sharp — far better than the p041 microfilm. Ink is even, the paper unstained, no damage, no manuscript marks. Almost every reading below is a fine-detail judgement, not a legibility problem. Layout: one running paragraph of 40 lines filling the whole column, no heading, no foot citation block, no signature, no catchword, no ornament. Body lines 1-40 continue the sentence begun on p041 and run on to p043.

the marginal note keyed p has NO marker anywhere in the body of this page. Lines 1-8 were checked letter by letter at 3-7x; the only wide gap (between 'rien' and 'valu' on line 1) is clean justification space with no ink at all. p041's last marker is {o}, so p is the expected next letter and the note is printed beside body line 1; either the sort was omitted or it belongs to p041's final line. Recorded as a note with key p and no marker, per conventions §4.

uncertain.text: relle peut prouenir auſsi d'eſtre chaſtré de nature, ou
uncertain.note: 'auſsi' here is long s + ROUND s, verified at 3x: the second letter is a short round s with no ascender. The same word is set with the ſſ ligature on lines[8] ('auſſi propre') and lines[20] ('aucuns auſſi'). The difference is deliberate compositor's practice, not a reading error; all three were checked separately.

uncertain.note: the point after the marker {u} is very lightly printed — a small speck at baseline between the italic u and the '&', far fainter than the solid points after {t} (lines[15]), {x} (lines[21]) and {y} (lines[26]). Read as a weakly inked period on the parallel of those three; reader B may read no punctuation there.

uncertain.text: ture demeure forcee {x}. Sur quoy quelques vns alleguẽt
uncertain.note: two pale brown horizontal marks sit over the 'u' of 'Sur' and over the 'uo' of 'quoy'. At 9x they are much lighter and thinner than the printed tildes on this page ('naturellemẽt', 'alleguẽt', 'cõtrainte') and are read as show-through/foxing, not tildes: 'Sũr' and 'quõy' are not words. Reader B may transcribe tildes here.

uncertain.text: neceſſité, que d'honneſte affection & vertu Chreſtiẽne.
uncertain.note: the mark over the second e of 'Chreſtiẽne' is a horizontal wavy bar (tilde), not the steeply slanted acute this font uses on 'chaſtré', 'né', 'entortilé'. Read as a tilde = 'Chreſtienne'. Reader B may read 'Chreſtiéne'.

three line breaks are printed with no word-break hyphen and are transcribed as printed: lines[5] 'contrain' + lines[6] 'te'; lines[13] 'cõtracté' is a whole word but lines[13]/lines[14] run on without one; margin note q likewise breaks 'par'/'tium.' unhyphenated. Hyphens are printed normally elsewhere on the page ('natu-', 'ſe-', 'char-', 'L'im-', 'violen-', 'na-', 'comman-', 'concupi-'), so these are compositor omissions.

spacing: the compositor repeatedly sets punctuation tight ('valu.L'impuiſſance', 'que,exprimer', 'honneſtes)ou', 'neceſſaires.q', 'eſtroitte,ou', 'paſſage,il', '&inualablemẽt') and sometimes with a space before ('nature , ou', 'cachee . L'impuiſſance', 'meres : &'), and sets 'ſemẽcecontrain' and 'la ſe-' solid. All normalized to single spaces per §1; no letter is added or removed.
set in spaced capitals and closed up here per §3. No terminal punctuation is printed after DV. The folio '42' stands at the left of the same line and matches the manifest.

the break sign after 'nou' is a short stroke set at mid x-height — higher than the round baseline point after 'ro' on the same line, but shorter than the clear hyphens of 'adil.e-', 'cõſultatio-', 'fraterni-', 'xxx-', 'ſic-'. Read as a hyphen ('nou-|uelles'); it could be read as a point. The same citation at p041 note b prints 'nou' with no break sign.

the numeral is three minims carrying three dots, the last descending: read 'iij'. The same citation at p041 note b reads 'col iiij.' (four), so the two pages disagree; 'iiij' cannot be wholly excluded, but only three dots and three strokes are visible at 10x.

printed solid as 'Gal.auxv.' There is a hair more space between 'u' and 'x' than between 'a' and 'u', and the sense requires 'au xv. li. de vſu. partium' (Galen, De usu partium, book XV), as the conventions' own example prints 'au xv. liur. de'. Split as 'au xv.' per the §1 word-division rule; 'aux v.' is the alternative reading.

the vowel after 'qu' is a single italic 'a' with no 'e' joined to it, so 'quaritur' is transcribed as printed; the Digest lemma is 'l. quaeritur', so an æ ligature (or a missing e) is what the compositor meant. Not modernized.

the mark between 'tatis' and 'de' sits low with a faint hook and could be a comma rather than a point. Read as a point, matching 'c. fraternitatis. de frig. & malef.' as the same citation is set in p041 (note l: 'c. laudabilẽ. de frig. & malef.').

the final point after 'vij' is very faint and small; included on the parallel of the other citation endings in this note. The numeral 'vij' carries two dots and a descending j, the same form as 'iij' at the start of the line.

the print sets 'l.lege .P. ſi'. The mark between 'lege' and 'P' is pale and irregular, much weaker than the crisp point after 'P' on the same line; read as a lightly inked point and normalized to 'lege. P.', but it may be an ink speck, in which case the line is 'l. lege P. ſi'. The matching faint point after 'mal' on lines[1] is clearer and is kept.
the first word is read 'mal' (three-stroke m, a, l); at this size 'nal' cannot be wholly excluded. With lines[2] it gives 'D. de ſicar.' (ad legem Corneliam de sicariis), which supports the reading.
no point is printed after the initial 'l'; checked at 10x, the gap between 'l' and 'ſi' is empty. Compare note r lines[0] 'l. quaritur.' and note x lines[0] 'l. lege', which both carry one.
